$comment: Reviewed, dated exceptions to the production dependency audit gate.
Enforced by scripts/audit-check.mjs, run by the `security` CI job.
An entry here means: we have looked at this advisory, we understand what it
would take to fix, and we have decided not to do that work before the date
given. It does NOT mean the advisory is wrong or harmless.
The gate fails if a production high/critical advisory has no entry, if an
entry is past its `expires` date, or if an entry no longer matches anything
(so the file cannot quietly accumulate dead suppressions).
Every entry below has the same root cause: the only available fix is a
major-version upgrade. `npm audit fix --force` would apply them, and would
take fastify from 4 to 5 across the whole gateway.
Dev-only advisories (vitest, vite, @vitest/coverage-v8, postcss, nanoid) are
not listed because the gate audits with --omit=dev. They are reported in the
job output and are a genuinely different risk class: none of them ship in a

advisories: GHSA-mrq3-vjjr-p77c (DoS via unbounded memory in sendWebStream)
GHSA-jx2c-rxcm-jvmq (Content-Type tab character bypasses body validation)
exceptions.reason: The gateway is built on fastify 4 and the upgrade also forces new majors of @fastify/jwt, cors, multipart and websocket, each with its own breaking changes. Partially mitigated already: the gateway sits behind an ingress that terminates TLS and sets X-Forwarded-*, and ALLOWED_ORIGINS is explicit rather than reflective in production. Scheduled as its own change, not folded into unrelated work.
Transitive through fastify; cannot be lifted independently. The deployed ingress does not expose HTTP/2 directly to the gateway pod. Fixed by the same upgrade as the entry above.

Transitive through @fastify/jwt. This is the one entry that genuinely warrants moving first, because it is in the token verification path. Tokens here are minted by this service alone with a single symmetric secret and no external issuer, which removes the confused-deputy shape most of these advisories rely on. Should be re-reviewed before the expiry rather than extended by habit.

Telemetry only. It processes spans this system produces about itself; it parses no attacker-controlled input on any request path. The jump spans many pre-1.0 releases with repeated API churn and would touch every file in packages/telemetry.
Transitive; same upgrade, same reasoning as above.
Transitive; same upgrade. The Jaeger propagator is not selected at runtime — packages/telemetry uses W3C trace context — so this code path is not exercised.
